description: This statement has three errors. Claim 1 prints the same physical therapy visit twice on one date, charging the $25 copay twice; claim 2 charges the member 20% for a lab test although note L1 says labs are covered in full; and claim 3's X-ray of the chest is dated two days after the statement date. A careful reviewer should flag the duplicate line, the lab charge and the impossible service date.

sources.what: An exact duplicate matches another claim line on beneficiary, provider, date of service, procedure code and billed amount
sources.source: CMS, Medicare Claims Processing Manual (Pub. 100-04), ch. 1, §120.2 Exact Duplicates, https://www.cms.gov/regulations-and-guidance/guidance/manuals/downloads/clm104c01.pdf

sources.what: Under the rule that a plan must state its cost sharing, this plan charges $0 for covered lab tests, as Original Medicare usually does (note L1)
sources.source: eCFR, 42 CFR 422.111(b)(2), Disclosure requirements (benefits and cost sharing), https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-IV/subchapter-B/part-422/subpart-C/section-422.111; Medicare.gov, Diagnostic laboratory tests, https://www.medicare.gov/coverage/diagnostic-laboratory-tests

sources.what: Compare each statement with your own calendar of appointments, tests and X-rays to check the dates
sources.source: Medicare.gov, Protecting Yourself From Fraud (CMS Product No. 10111), https://www.medicare.gov/publications/10111-protecting-yourself-from-fraud.pdf

sources.what: A Medicare Advantage plan mails an EOB each month you visit a provider, summarizing your claims and costs
sources.source: Medicare.gov, Checking the status of a claim, https://www.medicare.gov/providers-services/claims-appeals-complaints/claims/check-status
